summary: File inherited šaḏi bəṯre as Preterit Intransitive while preserving sense 4.
rationale: The qaṭəl-shaped alternative is distinct from L-series šḏele; this repairs form classification without deleting a numbered sense.

summary: Assign the pursuit example to the existing pursuit sense
rationale: Sense 2 already means '(bəṯr-) hinter jm. herstürzen, ihn verfolgen'. The example 'šaḏi bəṯre' has exactly that construction and is currently assigned to the repeated sense 4.

summary: Move the carding example with -wa to Infectum-wa
rationale: 'Šoḏǝnwa' contains the habitual-past -wa suffix, and the translation is 'They used to card earlier'. It belongs in Infectum-wa, retaining stem I and sense 1. The destination box is not yet present in this stem.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Famine/19)

data.translation: Yes, we used to card with a bow, cotton.

rationale: Thin carding Infectum-wa cell: explicit bow and cotton; existing -wa example is being refiled, not treated as unattested.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Famine/26)

data.translation: Then we would card cotton like so; we would card …

rationale: Thin carding Infectum-wa cell: overt cotton object within a detailed craft description.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Famine/30)

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa cell: carding is distinguished from spinning and washing in a craft sequence.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 2 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.51/2493)

data.turoyo: šuḏanwo bəṯrayye bak kefe, gurm w hay gurm (gaḥxo), bəṯrayye matəhiwonne.
data.translation: they would rush after them with stones, bang and another bang (laughter), they would drive them away.

rationale: Infectum-wa already exists for carding after round 1, but pursuit sense 2 is still empty; overt bəṯr target and stone instrument. Supplied English is project machine translation, not an edition translation; the reading rests on the Turoyo.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (Jan 2.3/423)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Əzzawo sədayye, šəġlowa, kətono, šəḏoyo mədone hawxa, šuġlo dan niše, əṯyowa, e.
data.translation: She would go to them, work, cotton, carding things like that, women's work, and come back, yes.

rationale: First I Infinitiv box: šəḏoyo in the explicit cotton/women’s-work list, distinct from the inherited Detransitive Part. Pass. šaḏyo. Supplied English is project machine translation, not an edition translation; the reading rests on the Turoyo.

summary: New sense 2b: (mit bəṯr-) jmndn. vertreiben, fortjagen
rationale: Two sources combine pursuit wording with controlled displacement, a destination or explicit exile.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (JTM 4.5/8)

data.turoyo: w dayəm bəṯrayna kšoḏe w aḥna bəṯre bəṯre na, kšəḏena bəṯre.
data.translation: Er jagt uns immer nach, und wir sind ihm immer auf den Fersen, wir jagen ihm nach.

rationale: Thin sense 2 Infectum cell: opposed pursuit with 3sg and reduced 1pl forms in one quotation.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (JTM 5.2/57)

data.turoyo: i naqqa dani kšoḏən, du aġayḏe kšoḏən bəṯranək, kmoḥe raġloṯe bu šuro komər didididididi…, w hanək d šoḏən bəṯrani kmiṭavəz.
data.translation: Wenn diese angreifen, wenn (die Kämpfer) ihres Aghas hinter den andern herjagen, schlägt er seine Füße gegen die Mauer und ruft didididididi; wenn aber jene hinter diesen herjagen, dann ist er wie gelähmt.

rationale: Thin pursuit Infectum cell: matched k- and unprefixed d- forms, all three tokens in one context.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (PrS 57/6)

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (PrS 50/40)

summary: example for sense 2b in Imperativ (103/50)

data.turoyo: Hawo li dukṯe, d moṭe u ḥəkm diḏux, šḏay bəṯre, lo saymat mede ebe <...>
data.translation: Diesen jage Weg an einen Ort, der unter deiner Herrschaft steht, tue ihm sonst nichts! <...>

rationale: First Imperativ of expulsion; destination and prohibition on further harm provide context.

summary: example for sense 2b in Preterit (106/24)

data.turoyo: Məlle: "Ya greʕo ṭowo, ġalabe rḥimo wayt ʕal lebi, yalanəz ono bu xabrawo, d məlluxli, ono šḏeli bəṯrux w səmlilux nafi bi arʕo."
data.translation: Dann sagte er: „Du guter Knecht, du warst meinem Herzen sehr teuer; nur wegen jenes Wortes, das du zu mir sagtest, habe ich dich vertrieben und dich auf Erden verbannt.‘

rationale: First Preterit of expulsion, with explicit following banishment statement.

summary: example for sense 3 in Imperativ (113/115)

data.turoyo: Kul ḥa ṭro madle daloqo d darbke, ayna, d kətle čuqmaq, ayna d kətle, moṭele ḥuḏo d nuro, de šḏayu b gawa!
data.translation: Jeder nehme ein brennendes Streichholz; oder wer ein Feuerzeug hat oder einen Kienspahn, der bringe ihn her und stecke ihn in den Haufen!

rationale: Thin sense 3 Imperativ cell: second command has omitted fire object and explicit inward target, unlike the already cited first command.

summary: Remove the repeated pursuit sense 4
rationale: Sense 4 repeats sense 2, including the pursuit meaning and bəṯr- construction. Keep sense 2 and remove this duplicate list item; the accompanying move-example proposal assigns its one example to sense 2.

summary: New idiom: šḏele/šoḏe səng w dawran baynoṯ- 'Verwirrung und Panik unter ... verbreiten'

data.headword: šḏele/šoḏe səng w dawran baynoṯ- 'Verwirrung und Panik unter ... verbreiten'
data.turoyo: B bə ʕAdoka hǧəmme laṭ ṭaye aʕlayna, šḏalle səng w u dawran baynoṯayna.
data.translation: Bei bĭ-ʿĂdoka griffen die Muslime uns an, sie verursachten Chaos und Panik unter uns.

rationale: One explicit verb + coordinated noun collocation; searches for dawran and səng found no matching collocation. Keep it outside numbered senses; first noun needs lexical confirmation.

summary: Preserve inherited I.2 and I.4 numbering even though both gloss pursuit. Their examples contrast L-series šḏele and qaṭəl-shaped šaḏi; the corpus predominantly supplies I.2-style Preterit and corresponding Infectum.

Overt l-agents in PrS 50/40 and 67/33 distinguish the chaser from the bəṯr target. PrS 2/28 remains ambiguous between l-agent dogs and dogs sent after game; it does not alone justify a causative sense.
MAC material supplies habitual carding in Infectum-wa and prospective carding in Infectum with object -le. The inherited Šoḏǝnwa token was present all along under the wrong box.
Two pursuit directions in JTM 4.5/8 and three tokens in JTM 5.2/57 are each shown in one quotation, without counting repeated text as multiple added examples.
Detransitive Part. Pass. šaḏyo at 65/305 is already quoted and describes carded cotton. No new finite Detransitive paradigm is established.
The panic collocation was mined separately from ordinary pursuit; read-only searches found no matching dawran expression, while səng alone also occurs with an unrelated tent-peg meaning under rfy.
III pursuit is already attested by the inherited mašḏe examples; none of these I occurrences requires reassignment to III.
All three occurrences checked. Existing senses 2 and 4 retain their numbers; the L-series pursuit token stays in 2. The round-1 correction of inherited Šoḏǝnwa to Infectum-wa is not proposed again.
šəḏoyo is an action nominal in a craft list with kətono, unlike attributive šaḏyo carded. Its evidence supports an Infinitiv box without another technical carding sense.
The English threw himself after at Jan 1.45/1973 adds a reflexive interpretation absent from the Turoyo; it is not used to establish valency and is not quoted.
Does the I.2/I.4 split encode the two Preterit patterns, a semantic distinction, or duplicate senses? Preserve both numbers pending editorial decision.
Confirm səng in JTM 3.1/3 and the conventionality of the coordinated panic expression; its combined context is clear but the individual first noun is not.
Does PrS 2/28 have l-marked dogs as agents or as recipients of a sending event?
Are the two expulsion contexts a conventional extension of bəṯr pursuit? The entry records them as 2b, with the contextual grounds explicit.
Should the inherited Detransitive Part. Pass. section receive an explicit separate numbered Detransitive gloss? The parser supplies none; only the attested participle is retained.
Confirm the citation form/vocalism of šəḏoyo at Jan 2.3/423 against the recording; preserve the source spelling rather than normalize it to the Detransitive participle.

Does the stone-pursuit clause Jan 1.51/2493 use a conventional expulsion extension, or is expulsion supplied only by the following matəhiwonne? Current filing conservatively keeps I.2 and records the contextual outcome.
Carding applies in cotton processing and in the broader textile work sequence; the inherited detailed gloss already allows fibres beyond cotton.
Pursuit with stones can culminate in driving thieves away, but matəhiwonne separately expresses that result. This alone does not reassign the chasing token to round-1 expulsion 2b.
